children: Eisai and Biogen reported five-year Clarity AD extension findings: 66% of low-tau patients showed no decline on CDR-SB and 62% improved. No new safety findings were observed; ARIA-E incidence was 0.6% in the fifth 12-month interval.
Long-term clinical benefit in earlier-stage patients supports lecanemab's potential durability.
Incidence was lower than the 13.5% first-year rate; the release reports no new safety findings.
At 5 years, CDR-SB difference was -2.05 vs ADNI
The comparison suggests sustained separation from natural-history decline, but relies on external data rather than a concurrent control.
351 patients received 5 years of continuous treatment
The long-term findings come from a subset of the original 1,795-patient trial.

This is a long-term extension update for an already approved Alzheimer’s treatment, adding evidence on durability and safety rather than announcing a new product or approval. Further commercial impact would depend on uptake and additional regulatory or clinical updates, neither quantified in this release.
Based on the original press release from Eisai Co., Ltd. distributed by Japan Corporate News.
